items.stem:
A café makes x litres of orange juice and y litres of mango juice each morning.
It makes at least 5 litres of orange juice.
It makes a total of at most 30 litres of juice.

parts.t: Write down an inequality in x for the amount of orange juice.
Write down an inequality in x and y for the total amount of juice.

sols: “At least 5 litres” means 5 litres or more.
The total amount of juice is x + y litres.

The region R is shaded on the grid.
It is bounded by the three lines y = 2, x = 7 and y = x.

parts.t: Write down the inequality given by the line y = 2.
Write down the inequality given by the line x = 7.
Write down the inequality given by the line y = x.

sols: Every point of R is on or above the horizontal line y = 2.
The lowest points of R, such as (5, 2), have y = 2.
the boundary is a solid line, so it is included
Every point of R is on or to the left of the vertical line x = 7.
The point (8, 3) is outside R, so it is not x ≥ 7.
Test (5, 3), which is inside R: 3 ≤ 5 is true.
substitute the point into the inequality
Test (3, 5), which is outside R: 5 ≤ 3 is false.

items.stem:
The region R is defined by the three inequalities
x ≥ 1    y ≥ 2    x + y ≤ 9.
x and y are integers.

parts.t: Write down the coordinates of the point in R with the largest possible value of x.
Find the largest possible value of x + 2y for a point in R.

sols: x is largest when y is as small as possible, so take y = 2.
x + 2y grows fastest with y, so make y as large as possible.
the coefficient of y is the larger one
Check the neighbouring corner points: (7, 2) gives 11 and (1, 2) gives 5, both smaller. ✓
ms:
M1 for identifying (1, 8) or for testing at least two vertices of R
A1
cao

items.stem:
x adults and y students go on a school trip.
There are at most 24 people altogether.
There are at least 3 adults.
The number of students is at least four times the number of adults.

parts.t: Write down an inequality for the total number of people.
Write down an inequality for the number of adults.
Write down an inequality connecting x and y for the last statement.

sols: The total number of people is x + y.
“At least 3 adults” means 3 or more adults.
Four times the number of adults is 4x.
The number of students, y, is at least this, so y ≥ 4x
be careful: the 4 multiplies the smaller quantity
Check with 4 adults and 16 students: 16 ≥ 4 × 4 ✓ and 4 + 16 = 20 ≤ 24 ✓

items.stem:
A workshop makes x tables and y chairs each week.
Each table uses 5 units of wood and each chair uses 2 units of wood. At most 60 units of wood are available.
Each table takes 2 hours to make and each chair takes 1 hour. At most 26 hours are available.
The workshop makes at least 4 tables.

parts.t: Write down an inequality for the wood.
Write down an inequality for the time.

The profit is $35 on each table and $15 on each chair.
Calculate the greatest possible profit.

sols: x tables use 5x units of wood and y chairs use 2y units.
x tables take 2x hours and y chairs take y hours.
The best point is where the two resource lines cross, so solve them together.
This satisfies x ≥ 4, so 8 tables and 10 chairs are allowed.
Check nearby points: (7, 12) gives $425 and (9, 7) gives $420, both smaller. ✓
ms:
M1 for identifying x = 8, y = 10 (or for evaluating 35x + 15y at two or more vertices)
A1
accept $430

The region R is shaded on the grid.
It is bounded by the three lines y = 1, y = 2x and x + y = 9.
x and y are integers.

parts.t: Write down the inequality given by the line y = 2x.
Write down the inequality given by the line x + y = 9.

T = 2x + 5y.
Find the maximum value of T for a point in R.

sols: R lies below and to the left of the line x + y = 9.
T = 2x + 5y grows fastest with y, so look for the point of R with the largest y.
That is where y = 2x meets x + y = 9: x + 2x = 9, so x = 3 and y = 6.

A tour company hires x small buses and y large buses.
It hires at most 12 buses altogether.
A small bus seats 15 people and a large bus seats 40 people. At least 250 seats are needed.
The number of small buses is at least twice the number of large buses.

parts.t: Write down an inequality for the number of buses.
Write down an inequality for the number of seats.
Write down an inequality connecting x and y for the last statement.

A small bus costs $80 to hire and a large bus costs $150.
Find the least possible total cost.

sols: The number of buses altogether is x + y.
x small buses give 15x seats and y large buses give 40y seats.
Twice the number of large buses is 2y.
the number of small buses is at least this
Only two combinations satisfy all three inequalities: (8, 4) and (9, 3).
The least possible total cost is $1170

items.stem:
Each day a baker makes x fruit cakes and y sponge cakes.
Each fruit cake uses 400 g of flour and each sponge cake uses 250 g of flour.
He has 10 kg of flour available.
He makes at least 10 fruit cakes.
He makes at least as many sponge cakes as fruit cakes.

parts.t: Write down an inequality for the number of fruit cakes.
Write down an inequality connecting x and y for the number of sponge cakes.
Show that the flour available gives the inequality 8x + 5y ≤ 200.
Find the greatest number of sponge cakes he can make in one day.

sols: “At least 10 fruit cakes” means 10 or more.
The number of sponge cakes, y, is at least the number of fruit cakes, x.
Divide every term by 50: 8x + 5y ≤ 200, as required
y is largest when x is smallest, so take x = 10.
The greatest number of sponge cakes is 24
ms:
M1 for 400x + 250y ≤ 10 000 oe (units consistent)
A1 for correct division by 50 shown

A shop orders x rucksacks and y sports bags.
The region R of possible orders is shaded on the grid.
x and y are integers.

parts.t: Write down the inequality given by the line x = 2.
Write down the inequality given by the line y = 2.
Write down the inequality given by the line x + y = 11.

The shop makes a profit of $9 on each rucksack and $5 on each sports bag.
Calculate the greatest possible profit.

The shop now also orders at least as many sports bags as rucksacks.
Write down the greatest possible profit now.

sols: R lies on or to the right of the line x = 2.
R lies on or above the line y = 2.
R lies on or below the line x + y = 11.
The point (6, 6) has 6 + 6 = 12 > 11 and is outside R.
Profit P = 9x + 5y. The coefficient of x is larger, so make x as large as possible.
The extra condition is y ≥ x, so (9, 2) is no longer allowed.
With y ≥ x and x + y ≤ 11, the largest x is 5, giving y = 6.
